headline: The 29 laws crystallize the atlas into emergent strata; hazards tighten across it, and protocols become ordered paths through the same structure.

concepts.name: Constraint Crystal
concepts.signature_moment: Five unlabeled strata emerge from the laws alone; only then do the S0–S4 rulers appear and reveal where computed rank agrees or disagrees.
concepts.what_happens: Over 900 ms, the 59 DOM tiles settle into a directed factor graph. Vertical position is topological rank computed only from prerequisite laws, horizontal position preserves family proximity, and the third axis separates crossing edges and alternative branches. Small non-text junctions encode AND as joined sockets and OR as open forks. High-in-degree elements sit above visibly broad prerequisite cones. Focusing a tile spreads its complete ancestor cone over 450 ms while unrelated edges retract. The camera stops after the initial settle; reduced motion shows the final layout with the same ancestor-cone inspection.
concepts.why_this_data: The 29 requires laws contain direction, conjunction and alternatives; they can generate rank independently of the existing depth field. Comparing that generated rank with S0–S4 tests whether depth is a discovered structural property rather than a decorative coordinate.
concepts.user_action: Scrub the graph formation, focus an element, and rotate within a constrained arc to inspect its prerequisite cone and OR branches.
concepts.they_now_understand: Deep elements are not merely assigned a higher label: they accumulate wider dependency cones, while alternative prerequisites make the atlas a family of possible graphs rather than one fixed DAG.
concepts.displaces: The tilted five-plane stack, fly-in, and depth-as-Z standing encoding.
concepts.failure_mode: If the laws are too sparse or contain unresolved cycles, the five strata do not emerge cleanly; operator junctions can also become visual punctuation without readable clauses.

concepts.name: Duplex Tension
concepts.signature_moment: The neutral dependency skeleton holds still while hazard-coloured chords appear above it, exposing a reflexive loop that closes across otherwise valid branches.
concepts.what_happens: The law graph remains an achromatic structure of straight directed struts. On hazard reveal, each of the 19 hazard rules grows simultaneously from both endpoints and meets as a curved cable 60–120 pixels above the skeleton over 600 ms. Height separates hazard cables from dependency edges; colour identifies hazard and line form distinguishes forbidden, elevated-risk and unverifiable. Selecting a cable lifts its endpoints and fades all other cables, leaving both edge sets legible in one fixed geometry.
concepts.why_this_data: Hazards are a second relation over exactly the same element nodes, but unlike requires edges they describe dangerous combinations between individually valid parts. A multiplex graph shows whether hazards reinforce, bridge or close cycles across the dependency structure.
concepts.user_action: Toggle the hazard edge set, select one rule, or isolate the hazards touching an element or protocol.
concepts.they_now_understand: Risk lives in relationships, not in red nodes; the dangerous composition can span distant dependency branches or turn a directed construction into a reflexive circuit.
concepts.displaces: A separate hazard list and any use of colour for family, depth or selection.
concepts.failure_mode: All 19 cables shown without height routing can resemble a red canopy; weak line-form differences can make hazard classes indistinguishable.

concepts.name: Protocol Braid
concepts.signature_moment: Two protocols unfurl as ordered tracks through the same element graph, merging at shared mechanisms and separating exactly where their architectures diverge.
concepts.what_happens: Selecting one of the 12 protocols grows a neutral ribbon through its member tiles in recorded necessity order, advancing one step every 120 ms and settling after the final element. The tiles never leave the shared graph. Adding a second protocol offsets its ribbon slightly in the third axis; shared memberships bundle into one thicker track, while unique members produce forks. Step numbers remain on the tiles, and nonmembers recede without disappearing. A static ordered ribbon is the reduced-motion artifact.
concepts.why_this_data: Each protocol is both a subset of the common 59-element vocabulary and an ordered construction history. Turning subsets into co-located tracks reveals reuse, shared prefixes and architectural divergence without inventing a separate coordinate system.
concepts.user_action: Choose one protocol, then add another for comparison or drag the sequence scrubber from first necessity to completed system.
concepts.they_now_understand: Protocols that look unrelated are recombinations of the same mechanisms, and their decisive differences occur at specific forks in an otherwise shared construction.
concepts.displaces: Pulling selected members into a camera-facing grid and relying on dimming plus isolated sequence numbers.
concepts.failure_mode: A poorly routed ribbon can imply that consecutive protocol steps are dependency-law edges; its rounded track must remain visually distinct from directed structural struts.

concepts.name: Fatal Chord
concepts.signature_moment: A dead protocol's ordered braid freezes intact, then one hazard-coloured chord snaps taut across it and identifies the composition that made the subset fatal.
concepts.what_happens: Choosing a dead protocol first draws its complete membership braid. After a 300 ms pause, only hazard relations contained within that subset rise from the graph. The known fatal relation tightens over 500 ms, pulling its endpoints a few pixels toward one another and pinching the braid at the failure site. A reflexive failure is shown with four accelerating, expanding pulses before a hard freeze, never as a smooth orbit. If a death lies outside the atlas's structural vocabulary, the braid remains unbroken and an empty cut marker states that no modeled edge explains it.
concepts.why_this_data: The dead protocols are known subsets with known break mechanisms, while the atlas deliberately distinguishes compositional hazards from implementation failures. The same node and edge vocabulary can therefore perform an autopsy without pretending to explain what it cannot represent.
concepts.user_action: Select a dead protocol, replay its construction, and stop at the fatal edge to inspect the participating elements and rule.
concepts.they_now_understand: A protocol can contain individually sound elements yet fail because one relation inside its chosen subset is fatal; absence of such an edge marks the atlas's implementation-level blind spot.
concepts.displaces: A textual post-mortem detached from the selected protocol and decorative loop animation.
concepts.failure_mode: Endpoint displacement can over-dramatize causality, and forcing an implementation-only death onto a hazard edge would make the visualization dishonest.

concepts.name: Choice Hinges
concepts.signature_moment: The user flips one OR fork from Sh to Ix; the prerequisite structure rethreads around the hinge while the downstream protocol remains recognizably the same machine.
concepts.what_happens: Every alternative clause becomes a draggable three-dimensional hinge. Pulling one alternative toward the clause socket over 350 ms disconnects the current branch, connects the replacement, recomputes the prerequisite closure, and relaxes affected nodes into new ranks over another 500 ms. Unchanged nodes stay pinned, making the structural consequence readable. With a protocol selected, its braid reroutes through the chosen substitute and unsupported members fold into a neutral side rail rather than vanishing.
concepts.why_this_data: The vertical bars inside the 29 laws mean the atlas does not specify one dependency graph; it specifies a space of valid graphs. Interactive hinges expose that latent design space and connect it directly to the 16 substitute families.
concepts.user_action: Drag an alternative into a law socket, compare the resulting closure, and restore the recorded protocol choice.
concepts.they_now_understand: Substitution is constrained: replacing one mechanism can preserve the downstream architecture, change its prerequisite burden, or invalidate part of the selected protocol.
concepts.displaces: Passive reading of OR notation and any generic free-rotation interaction.
concepts.failure_mode: The recomputed graph may jump, imply choices the source laws do not authorize, or overwhelm users if several clauses change simultaneously.

the_one_to_build: Constraint Crystal — it makes the laws the generator of the spatial form, gives the third dimension a real edge-routing job, and establishes one stable geometry for every later hazard and protocol view.
what_everyone_will_get_wrong: They will map S0–S4 directly onto Z and call that data-driven; the stronger move is to derive rank from the laws, reserve three-dimensional separation for logic and crossings, then test depth against what emerges.
